All primary units (54-61) are test-only changes. Test stub LanguageModel.prepare signatures move from (input, cache, windowSize:) to (input, cache, state: LMOutput.State?, prefill: PrefillParameters) in StandaloneServerTests.swift:663, LoadedModelsStoreTests.swift:104, ProviderModelSwitchTests.swift:699, StandaloneEvictionOwnershipTests.swift:34 and StartupPreloadTests.swift:885. LaunchAgentRestartTests.swift:3 changes to `@testable import MLXLMCommon`. The stubs return .tokens(input.text) and hold no keys, weights or prompt data. They add no production attack surface and touch no TB-002, TB-009, TB-011, A-003 or T-041 behavior.

The replayed integration source shows the production side. It is a submodule bump of libs/mlx, libs/mlx-swift and libs/mlx-swift-lm, with a changelog and docs path updates. GLM5NextProtectedExecution.swift forwards state and prefill unchanged to root.prepare. MLXLLM-qualified Gemma4AssistantDraftModel.load calls are updated in three files. ModelBenchmark.swift ignores the new .rejectedToolCall event, which is benchmark-only. Nothing in the supplied evidence shows a regression.

The replay is incomplete (265 units omitted). The submodule pointers' content (Metal kernels, the new prefill/state semantics, the rejected tool-call event handling in the production tool path, the Qwen 3.5 sanitize throw) is not visible. A later pass should check, if possible, that the upstream sync does not change KV/prefix-cache scoping or cacheSalt handling (T-041), and that the tool-call rejection path does not leak plaintext or fail open (T-008). Coverage of the dependency bump is limited by the missing source, and that gap does not show the bump is safe. This does not affect the test-only conclusion for the primary units.
